message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the federal holidays in Canada that create **long weekends** in 2023. (A long weekend is defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, giving you a three‑day break.)

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Long Weekend Period |
|---------|--------------|---------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday, Jan 1 | **Dec 31 – Jan 2** (observed Monday) |
| Good Friday | Friday, Apr 7 | **Apr 7 – Apr 9** |
| Victoria Day | Monday, May 22 | **May 20 – May 22** |
| Canada Day | Saturday, Jul 1 (observed Monday, Jul 3) | **Jul 1 – Jul 3** |
| Labour Day | Monday, Sep 4 | **Sep 2 – Sep 4** |
| Thanksgiving | Monday, Oct 9 | **Oct 7 – Oct 9** |
| Christmas Day | Monday, Dec 25 | **Dec 23 – Dec 25** |

> **Note:**  
> • Some provinces observe additional holidays that can create long weekends (e.g., Family Day in Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Ontario; Heritage Day in Ontario; etc.).  
> • Remembrance Day (Nov 11) is a federal holiday but does not create a long weekend in 2023 because it falls on a Wednesday.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the provincial long weekends for a specific province!
